subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should after_compaction hooks receive a permanent current-session reset API, and if so must the legacy explicit-current-key call remain part of the supported plugin contract?
rationale: This creates compatibility-sensitive plugin API and session-lifecycle behavior; code review can reject unsafe authority propagation but cannot decide which external call shape OpenClaw intends to support permanently.

options.title: Approve the scoped API
options.body: Keep reason-only resetSession as canonical, retain the explicit-current-key form only as a documented compatibility overload, and prevent raw reset authority from crossing plugin boundaries.

options.title: Require reason-only API
options.body: Remove the explicit-key overload and require affected plugins to migrate before this capability ships.

options.title: Pause the API
options.body: Withhold hook-driven resets until maintainers choose a different generic lifecycle capability or plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped API
recommendation.body: Keep reason-only resetSession as canonical, retain the explicit-current-key form only as a documented compatibility overload, and prevent raw reset authority from crossing plugin boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for the affected external contract is the introduction of the compaction/reset hook family.
